questions.q: Why isn't simply prompting a model to "reply with only JSON" reliable enough for production code?
options: It usually works, but isn't guaranteed — stray text or malformed JSON can still slip through
Models are physically incapable of producing JSON without a special field
It only works for very short responses
It requires a paid add-on to function at all
questions.explain: Plain prompting is probabilistic, not guaranteed — which is exactly the gap structured-output features close.

questions.q: How does Anthropic's output_config.format feature guarantee schema compliance?
options: It validates the output after generation and retries on failure
It constrains which tokens the model can generate during generation itself
It runs a separate model to fix malformed JSON
It strips any text that doesn't look like JSON from the response
questions.explain: This is constrained decoding — the schema restricts token generation in real time, not a post-hoc check.

questions.q: When using output_config.format, where does the resulting JSON string land in the response?
options: In a dedicated json field at the top level
In content[0].input
In content[0].text, as a JSON string
In the usage object
questions.explain: The reply is still an ordinary text content block — its text value is a JSON string guaranteed to match the schema.

questions.q: In the forced-tool-call pattern for structured output, where does the parsed result land?
options: content[0].input, already parsed as an object
content[0].text, as a raw string
A separate /tool_result endpoint response
It is not accessible from the API response
questions.explain: Forcing a tool call puts the structured data directly in content[0].input — already parsed, with no string-decoding step.

questions.q: What does stop_reason: "refusal" indicate in a structured-output response?
options: The request succeeded and is ready to parse
The model declined to produce output matching the schema
The connection was dropped mid-stream
The schema itself was invalid JSON
questions.explain: refusal specifically means the model declined to generate schema-conforming output, distinct from end_turn (success) or max_tokens (cut off).
